title: Streaming downloads can hang indefinitely and leak response handles

evidence.quote:
response = self.session.get(
    endpoint,
    params=search_params,
    timeout=self.timeout,
    allow_redirects=False,
)

reasoning: The search and document metadata paths set a timeout and close responses in finally blocks, but download_document_image omits both. A slow or stalled image server can block the full search pipeline forever despite MAX_DOWNLOAD_RETRIES, because the first stream may never time out. Successful and failed streamed responses are also not explicitly closed, which can leave connections/file descriptors held in the session pool across many page downloads.
reproduction: Run the full search against an image URL served by a test HTTP server that accepts the connection and never sends the body. download_document_image blocks inside session.get/iter_content instead of timing out and retrying.
recommendation: Pass timeout=self.timeout or a connect/read timeout tuple to the streaming GET and use a context manager, e.g. with self.session.get(..., stream=True, timeout=self.timeout) as response. Also clean up partial output files when a download fails mid-stream.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests cover archive image downloads, retry behavior, or stalled HTTP responses.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test using a local fake server or mocked requests.Session.get that raises a read timeout during iter_content, then assert the method retries, closes the response, and returns False without leaving a partial file.
minimumFixScope: ArchiveAPIClient.download_document_image download loop and failure cleanup.
